name: Memory Recurrence
seeded_conditions_note: The five strings above are section 20.4's own arm list, copied without addition. How each is planted on this estate: memory off and memory on are the BM_MEMORY seam scripts/memory_ab.py already drives, one run per task per mode; stale memory is a seeded lesson whose applies_to names a path that no longer exists in the tree, the exact shape scripts/test_recall_revalidation.py drives; contradictory memory is a seeded lesson asserting the opposite of what the current source says, planted so the evidence hierarchy of Zone 4 can be observed choosing; superseded memory is a lesson carrying a superseded_by pointer to a newer one, both retrievable, so the run must apply the newer. Every arm runs the same frozen task set so the arms differ only in what memory holds.

fairness_notes.starting repository: One frozen repository and one frozen memory store per arm, both rebuilt from the same snapshot before each arm so an earlier arm cannot teach a later one.
fairness_notes.model where possible: The same model id across all five arms. A memory result measured across two models measures the models.
fairness_notes.token budget: One ceiling per task per arm. A memory-on arm that wins by spending twice as much has not won the same thing.
fairness_notes.task instruction: The task set is DATA, frozen in a JSON file the way benchmarks/memory-ab/tasks-2026-08-30.json already is, and passed identically to every arm.
fairness_notes.hardware/environment: One machine, hooks in the same state, the recall hook wired identically except for the seam under test.
fairness_notes.maximum human interventions: Zero. A human hint about a lesson would be the lesson.
fairness_notes.scoring rubric before execution: scoring_rubric below is frozen with this file, including each task's own check command.

metrics.proved: The instrument is built and proven honest: driven once over the real logs it printed 'recall off: 434 session(s), 60851 tool call(s), 0 lesson(s) shown, 0 repeat(s)' and refused to compose a comparison, exiting 2 with NO-DATA on the other arm.
metrics.gap: Row E53 is OPEN precisely because both arms have not filled. The counter that exists measures lessons shown and repeats observed in real session logs; the controlled two week comparison it was built for has not run. scripts/e53_lesson_ab.py is the fast lab version of the same question and has run once, on eight tasks per arm.

metrics.proved: The harness records a duration per task per mode and writes it into benchmarks/memory-ab/results-2026-08-30.json.
metrics.gap: In the one real run those durations measured a file replay, not the model, and the result document says so and treats the column as NO-DATA. Time to correction, which is what section 20.4 asks for, needs the arms run live rather than replayed.

metrics.proved: A seeded lesson whose applies_to names a path absent from the tree is recalled, refused by name with the line 'recall: STALE <slug>: anchor <x> not found in <tree>; not applied', and is absent from the applied section of the receipt, while a current lesson is applied. This is the false-memory-induced failure of section 20.4, measured as a refusal.

Each task carries its own check command and the harness scores every task in every mode by that check's exit code; the first real run reported per mode success of 4 of 11 off and 11 of 11 on, with the harness exiting 0.

Four of the six measures the run could not honestly fill were written into the result rows as NO-DATA strings naming the reason, for example 'NO-DATA: no mistake ledger is wired to compare against', rather than left blank or filled with a zero.

measures_outside_the_fifteen.would_require: Zone 4 ranks current evidence above verified memory above unverified recall. The stale case is enforced and tested. The contradictory case, where a retrievable lesson disagrees with what the source says right now and the source must win, has no test of its own, so this arm reports NO-DATA until one exists.

rules: Each task is scored by its own frozen check command's exit code, never by reading the output.
A lift is claimed only as a property of this task set, named with its n. The task set is published with the result.
A stale, contradictory or superseded lesson that reaches the applied section of the receipt fails the arm outright, whatever the task score.
A refusal that names the stale lesson counts as a pass for that arm, because the required behaviour is refusal, not silence.
Repeated failure is counted per failure class, from the ledger, never from an impression of the transcript.
Any measure the run cannot fill honestly is written NO-DATA with its reason in the result row itself.

text: the agent can explain which lesson influenced the run
win_condition.met_when: All five statements hold on the frozen task set, each from a published arm record, with the fifth read off the receipt's own applied-memory section rather than from prose.

raw_artifacts.rule: Publish raw artifacts. Do not publish only a synthetic score.
